findings.title: Custom approval rule: deals above $25,000 need a sales manager's approval before they can be won
findings.detail: custom/modules/Opportunities/DealApproval.php runs before every save of an opportunity, from the edit screen, inline edit, mass update, import or the API. It compares the US-dollar value (amount_usdollar), not the amount typed in. Only a user with the role 'Sales Manager' who shares a team (security group) with the deal's salesperson, or an administrator, can approve or reject. A blocked 'Closed Won' keeps the previous stage and sets the approval to Requested. Approving records who, when and the approved US-dollar amount; raising the amount afterwards withdraws the approval. In the data: 20 deals approved, 12 waiting, 1 rejected; approvals by mchen (14), ohaddad (6). 2 deals above the threshold were won without an approval, all closed before 2020: the rule checks the moment a deal is closed, it does not re-check old deals. Not part of standard SuiteCRM: added under custom/.

evidence.db: SELECT approval_status_c, COUNT(*) FROM opportunities JOIN opportunities_cstm ... GROUP BY approval_status_c

messages.not_manager: Only a sales manager on this team can approve or reject a deal.
messages.withdrawn: The amount is now above the approved amount, so the approval was withdrawn.
messages.blocked: Deals above $25,000 need approval from a sales manager before they can be marked Closed Won. Approval has been requested.

findings.title: 1 open deal(s) look below $25,000 but need approval, because the rule converts to US dollars
findings.detail: 'Blue Bird Dental Group - Euro-priced cold-chain or' is EUR 24,000, worth $26,086.96. A rebuild that compared the amount as typed would let it be won without approval. The new workspace must keep the stored US-dollar value and its conversion.

evidence.db: SELECT name, amount, amount_usdollar, iso4217 FROM opportunities JOIN currencies ... WHERE amount <= 25000 AND amount_usdollar > 25000

result.name: Blue Bird Dental Group - Euro-priced cold-chain or

findings.title: 19 accounts in 9 groups have near-identical names but are different customers
findings.detail: For example 'Bluebird Dental' (East Sales, 3 contacts, 2 deals), 'Blue Bird Dental Group' (West Sales, 4 contacts, 2 deals). Each has its own contacts and deals. Moving the data must keep them apart, and converting a lead must not link it to a look-alike account.

evidence.db: accounts whose normalised names are equal, or at least 0.8 alike with the same first five letters

findings.title: 36 contact names appear at more than one account
findings.detail: Nadia Adeyemi (2 accounts), Amara Adeyemi (2 accounts), Victor Adeyemi (2 accounts), Olivia Bennett (2 accounts), Mei Brennan (2 accounts), Lucia Cohen (2 accounts) and 30 more. Each is linked to its own account; they must not be merged.

evidence.db: SELECT first_name, last_name, COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) FROM contacts JOIN accounts_contacts ... HAVING > 1

findings.title: Access is limited by 3 roles and 2 teams
findings.detail: Sales Manager: view team, edit team, delete team (accounts); Salesperson: view team, edit own, delete none (accounts); Support: view all, edit none, delete none (accounts). 'team' means the record belongs to one of the user's security groups or is assigned to them; 'own' means assigned to them. Records join a team when created (settings: additive=True, inherit_assigned=True, inherit_creator=True, inherit_parent=True). 1,791 sales records are in a team. These restrictions are standard SuiteCRM features, configured by the customer.

evidence.db: SELECT r.name, a.category, a.name, ra.access_override FROM acl_roles_actions ra JOIN acl_actions a ... JOIN acl_roles r ...

findings.title: Support cases, meetings and calls point at sales records
findings.detail: Cases → Accounts: 60 (on 47 accounts); Meetings → Accounts: 38; Meetings → Opportunities: 72; Calls → Accounts: 53; Calls → Leads: 27; Notes on cases → Cases: 30; Tasks on cases → Cases: 20; Cases → Contacts: 60. If the sales records move, these links cross the boundary between the new workspace and SuiteCRM.

evidence.db: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cases JOIN accounts ON accounts.id = cases.account_id WHERE cases.deleted = 0

findings.title: 231 sales records belong to users who are no longer active
findings.detail: Accounts: 20, Contacts: 46, Leads: 2, Opportunities: 34, Notes: 87, Tasks: 42. SuiteCRM keeps them assigned; their team can still see them.

evidence.db: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM <table> JOIN users ON users.id = assigned_user_id WHERE users.status <> 'Active'

findings.title: 6 soft-deleted records are still in the database
findings.detail: SuiteCRM marks deleted records with deleted = 1 and hides them: Accounts: 2, Contacts: 3, Opportunities: 1.

evidence.db: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM <table> WHERE deleted = 1

findings.title: Lead conversion: 22 leads converted; activities stay on the lead
findings.detail: Converting a lead creates a contact and links or creates an account, optionally a deal (7 of the converted leads have one). The setting lead_conv_activity_opt = 'donothing' leaves the lead's notes and tasks on the lead.

evidence.db: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM leads WHERE converted = 1

findings.title: SuiteCRM 7.11.23 needs PHP 7.4 or older and MariaDB 10.3 / MySQL 8.0 or older
findings.detail: 7.11.23 (2021-11-19) is the last 7.11 release. PHP 7.4 reached end of life on 2022-11-28 and MariaDB 10.3 on 2023-05-25. SuiteCRM 7 itself is now at 7.15.2.

findings.title: config.php contains the database password in plain text
findings.detail: Normal for SuiteCRM, but the file must not be shared or committed. We redacted it in everything we store; rotate it after the move.

findings.title: No SuiteCRM file was changed; 18 customer files under custom/ (field settings 6, layout 6, labels 4, code 1, hook registration 1)
findings.detail: Checked 9,546 files against the checksums SuiteCRM ships in files.md5. Customizations live in custom/ (1124 lines written by the customer or Studio, plus files compiled by Quick Repair).
